definition: The natural shedding of a plant part, especially the dropping of leaves, fruit, or flowers; also, a cutting off or separation.
etymology: From Latin abscissio, “a cutting away,” from abscindere: ab- “away” plus scindere “to cut or split.” In autumn, a tree makes this old act of cutting at the base of each leaf stem.
usage: By mid-September, abscission had begun at the edges of the poplar grove.
